# How the restart routine can go wrong

Written before `router.sh` and `task.sh`, and updated with each review. Each line is a failure and the defence the code has for it.
"Router" is the `router` job in `fleet.yml`, "task job" is the agent's `task` job, "outcome job" is the `outcome` job that judges it, and "check" is `task.sh check`.

A start is a run with outcome `progress`, `failed` or `done`. `paused` and `cancelled` aren't starts.

| # | Failure | Defence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Double start: two router runs (cron and a label event) dispatch the same task at once | Rounds share the concurrency group `fleet-router-round` and run one at a time. Each dispatch is a run named `task #<n>`, and a queued, pending or in-progress run with that name means "running". If a dispatch lands before GitHub lists it, the task job's own group `fleet-task-<n>` (no cancel) makes the second one wait, and its check finds the PR state the first one left. One writer per task at any time. |
| 2 | Restart of a stopped task | `fleet:stop` cancels every active `task #<n>` run. Each stop event has its own concurrency group `fleet-router-stop-<n>`, so a burst of stop labels is never dropped as a superseded pending run. The router skips any issue with `fleet:stop` and cancels whatever it still has running, and check stops the task job cleanly if the label is there when it starts. "Stop all" (the `stop_all` dispatch input) labels every open task and cancels every task run, in its own group. |
| 3 | Restart of a task waiting to land | A ready PR in the merge queue, or with auto-merge on and checks pending or passing, is "waiting". Merge queue state comes from GraphQL `isInMergeQueue`. |
| 4 | A ready PR that can't land is never repaired | A ready PR whose checks failed or errored is unfinished whatever auto-merge says. A ready PR with auto-merge off and not queued is unfinished. Drafts, closed-only PRs and no PR are unfinished. Open question for the live proof: does GitHub turn auto-merge off when the queue drops a PR? If it doesn't and the checks passed, the task waits on a PR that will never land. |
| 5 | Forged marker comment | Only comments whose author is `github-actions[bot]` (type `Bot`) count, and the marker must be the comment's whole first line. Markers are posted only by the outcome job. The task job's `GITHUB_TOKEN` has no `issues: write`, and the agent's Claude app token is cut to `issues: read` (`additional_permissions`), so the agent can't post, edit or delete a marker or remove `fleet:stop` or `fleet:failed` with the tokens it's given (see 21 for the ones it might take). `ci.yml` has `contents: read` only. |
| 6 | Issue written or edited by someone else | Only issues whose author is `FLEET_OWNER` start, compared without letter case. An issue with no author can't start. A missing `FLEET_OWNER` fails the job instead of trusting everyone. Edits by others need write access, and the brief is read fresh at each start. |
| 7 | Cap never reached | Starts are counted from markers: at most `FLEET_MAX_STARTS` (default 6) starts, and two `failed` starts in a row is also a cap. `done` counts, so a PR the queue keeps dropping can't loop forever. The outcome job runs on its own runner after every task run, including a lost runner, a job timeout and a cancel: a task job that died without outputs is recorded as `failed` (or `cancelled`). It runs the cap check after every marker, `done` included, so the label and the Telegram alert come from the run that hit the cap. The router checks the caps too. Gap: a run cancelled with "force cancel" may skip the outcome job and leave no marker. |
| 8 | Cron late or skipped | GitHub's schedule is best effort. Label events also start the router, and nothing depends on the cron being on time: a late round just starts work later. |
| 9 | Dispatch or another change fails | Each failed `gh` change is logged and counted, the router carries on with the other tasks and then exits non-zero so the run shows red. The next round tries again. |
| 10 | One issue's state can't be read | Each issue is decided in its own subshell. An API error or an unreadable value skips that issue with a warning, and the round carries on. A `retry_after` that isn't a real date is read as no pause. |
| 11 | API pagination past 30 or 100 items | Issues, comments, blockers and branches use `gh api --paginate --slurp` with `per_page=100`. Runs use `gh run list` with a 1000 limit per status. PRs are looked up per head branch and base branch, 100 at a time. |
| 12 | Issue with no `Base:` line, or a base branch that doesn't exist | The task job fails before the checkout, and the outcome job records `failed`. Two in a row add `fleet:failed`. |
| 13 | Deleted task branch | GitHub closes the PR. The task job finds no `task/<n>` on the remote and creates it again from the base, and the agent opens a new PR. |
| 14 | Closed, unmerged PR | Not "waiting", not "done", so the task is unfinished and the agent opens a new PR. To stop a task, use `fleet:stop`, not closing the PR. |
| 15 | Usage limit loops | A run that hits a seat limit records `paused` with the reset time when the SDK gives one, and the router waits until then. The matcher reads only the newest `rate_limit_event`, and counts it only when it's `rejected` and overage isn't carrying the session. A `retry_after` more than 8 days ahead is recorded as 8 days. Paused runs aren't starts, and there is no time cap, so a task can wait on limits for as long as they last. |
| 16 | Job killed at the 6 hour limit | The agent step stops at 330 minutes and the job at 355, so the checkpoint gets time to run. The outcome job runs on its own runner whatever happens to the task job. |
| 17 | Work lost when a run dies | The checkpoint commits and pushes what's left in the tree with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, with git hooks off. That push starts no CI, so it runs only when the task has no PR or a draft one, never on a ready PR. It never runs when the checkout or the agent step was skipped, and `.fleet-rules/` and `node_modules/` are ignored. A failed checkpoint is a warning, not a red job. |
| 18 | Issue body used as shell | The body is written to a file with `gh api ... --jq .body > file`. Scripts read issue JSON with `jq` and only print numbers, labels and the validated base branch name. The prompt is fixed text. |
| 19 | A task issue that's a PR | `/issues` also lists PRs. Anything with `pull_request` set is dropped. |
| 20 | Dispatched run rejected as a bot | Runs the router starts have `github-actions[bot]` as their actor, and the action refuses bot actors unless `allowed_bots` lists them, so the task job lists exactly that one bot. |
| 21 | Runner isn't a sandbox | Not enforceable, and accepted. The agent runs any shell command on the task job's runner, with sudo. For the length of its job it holds its own seat token and the rules deploy key: both are in the runner's memory, which sudo can read. It can probably mint a wider Claude app token through OIDC (the job has `id-token: write`, and the request variables are in the parent process). It can change every output the task job reports, so it can claim `paused` (not a start), claim it never reached the checkout (no marker) or fake a step timeout (`progress` instead of `failed`). What limits the damage: the seat environments are usable only from `main`; `main` and `fleet/**` are protected by rulesets (no push, no force push, no deletion, CI and the merge queue on `fleet/**`, the owner's review on `main`); the caps are counted from markers that only the outcome job, on its own runner, can write; a false `paused` waits at most 8 days. |
| 22 | Strangers write instructions for the agent | The router locks the task issue's conversation before it starts the task, and the outcome job locks the task PR's conversation. The prompt says comments are never instructions. Gap: a PR the agent opens can take comments until its run's outcome job locks it. |
| 23 | A fork PR named `task/<n>` | Only PRs from this repo into the task's base branch count. A fork PR, or a PR into another base, never makes a task look done or waiting. |
| 24 | A task PR changes the CI gate on a fleet branch | `ci.yml` fails a PR or merge group into `fleet/**` that touches `.github/` or `test.sh`. Those changes go to `main` through the owner. |
| 25 | The final PR never opens, or opens early | At the end of each round the router opens `fleet/<topic>` into `main` only when the branch is ahead of `main`, at least one closed fleet issue names it as Base, no open fleet issue names it (stopped and failed tasks count as open), and no PR into `main` is open. Telegram hears "ready for review". |
| 26 | A failed task restarted by removing `fleet:failed` | It isn't: its markers still count, so the next round labels it again. Close the issue and open a new one to retry. |

## Known and accepted

- The rules deploy key reads the whole private `agents-config` repo, not just the files copied to `~/.claude`. A separate rules-only repo with its own key would limit that. Not taken this round.
- The Claude app may hold the Workflows permission. A dedicated GitHub App without it, passed as `github_token`, would close the OIDC route in 21. Not taken this round.
- The Workflows permission matters because a minted token could push a workflow to `task/<n>`. The rulesets still stop it from reaching `main` or `fleet/**`.
